title: ID S1297: Adds to existing law to establish the Conversational AI Safety Act.

obligations: If reasonable persons would be misled to believe that they are interacting with a human, an operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose that the conversational AI service is artificial intelligence (48-2103(1)).

An operator shall adopt a protocol for the conversational AI service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation that includes making reasonable efforts to provide a response that refers users to crisis service providers such as a suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis services (48-2103(2)).

An operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to minor account holders that they are interacting with artificial intelligence, either as a persistent visible disclaimer or both at the beginning of each session and appearing at least every three hours in a continuous conversational AI service interaction (48-2104(1)).

For minor account holders, an operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the conversational AI service from producing visual material of sexually explicit conduct, generating direct statements that the account holder should engage in sexually explicit conduct, or generating statements that sexually objectify the account holder (48-2104(3)).

For minor account holders, an operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent a conversational AI service from generating statements that would lead reasonable persons to believe that they are interacting with a human, including explicit claims that the conversational AI service is sentient or human, statements that simulate emotional dependence, statements that simulate romantic or sexual innuendos, or role playing of adult minor romantic relationships (48-2104(4)).

An operator shall offer tools for minor account holders and, where such account holders are under thirteen years of age, their parents or guardians, to manage the account holder's privacy and account settings; an operator shall also offer related tools to the parents or guardians of minor account holders thirteen years of age and older, as appropriate based on relevant risks (48-2104(5)).
prohibitions: An operator shall not knowingly and intentionally cause or program a conversational AI service to make any representation or statement that explicitly indicates that the conversational AI service is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care (48-2103(3)).

Where an operator knows or has reasonable certainty that an account holder is a minor, the operator shall not provide the user with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with the intent to encourage increased engagement with the conversational AI service (48-2104(2)).

What it does

The Conversational AI Safety Act requires operators of conversational AI services accessible to the general public to disclose when users may be misled into thinking they are interacting with a human, to adopt a protocol for responding to suicidal ideation, and to avoid claiming to provide professional mental health care. It imposes additional requirements for minor account holders, including disclosures, limits on engagement rewards, and measures to prevent sexual content and human impersonation. It provides for enforcement by the attorney general through injunctions and civil penalties.

Who it applies to

  • Operators, meaning persons who develop and make available a conversational AI service to the public, excluding mobile application stores and search engines solely because they provide access (48-2102(6)).

Effective date

July 1, 2027 (Sec. 2).

Key definitions

  • Account holder: an individual who has or opens an account or profile to use a conversational AI service (48-2102(1)).
  • Conversational AI service: an artificial intelligence software application, web interface, or computer program that is accessible to the general public and that primarily simulates human conversation and interaction through textual, visual, or aural communications; it does not include software primarily designed and marketed for use by developers or researchers, a feature within another software application that is not a conversational AI service, software designed to provide outputs relating to a narrow and discrete topic, software primarily designed and marketed for commercial use by business entities including employees, contractors, or clients whether delivered via cloud, on premises, or hybrid deployments, software designed to function as a speaker and voice command interface or voice activated virtual assistant for a consumer electronic device, software used by a business solely for internal purposes, or software accessible only to individuals who have entered into a commercial agreement, enterprise contract, or similar business arrangement with the operator (48-2102(2)).
  • Individual: a natural person (48-2102(3)).
  • Minor: an individual under circumstances where an operator has actual knowledge or reasonable certainty that the individual is under eighteen years of age (48-2102(4)).
  • Minor account holder: an account holder who is a minor (48-2102(5)).
  • Operator: a person who develops and makes available a conversational AI service to the public; operator does not include mobile application stores or search engines solely because they provide access to a conversational AI service (48-2102(6)).
  • Person: a natural person or legal entity (48-2102(7)).
  • Sexually explicit conduct and visual depiction: have the same meanings as provided in 18 U.S.C. 2256 (48-2102(8)).

Obligations

  • If reasonable persons would be misled to believe that they are interacting with a human, an operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose that the conversational AI service is artificial intelligence (48-2103(1)).
  • An operator shall adopt a protocol for the conversational AI service to respond to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation that includes making reasonable efforts to provide a response that refers users to crisis service providers such as a suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis services (48-2103(2)).
  • An operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to minor account holders that they are interacting with artificial intelligence, either as a persistent visible disclaimer or both at the beginning of each session and appearing at least every three hours in a continuous conversational AI service interaction (48-2104(1)).
  • For minor account holders, an operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent the conversational AI service from producing visual material of sexually explicit conduct, generating direct statements that the account holder should engage in sexually explicit conduct, or generating statements that sexually objectify the account holder (48-2104(3)).
  • For minor account holders, an operator shall institute reasonable measures to prevent a conversational AI service from generating statements that would lead reasonable persons to believe that they are interacting with a human, including explicit claims that the conversational AI service is sentient or human, statements that simulate emotional dependence, statements that simulate romantic or sexual innuendos, or role playing of adult minor romantic relationships (48-2104(4)).
  • An operator shall offer tools for minor account holders and, where such account holders are under thirteen years of age, their parents or guardians, to manage the account holder's privacy and account settings; an operator shall also offer related tools to the parents or guardians of minor account holders thirteen years of age and older, as appropriate based on relevant risks (48-2104(5)).

Prohibitions

  • An operator shall not knowingly and intentionally cause or program a conversational AI service to make any representation or statement that explicitly indicates that the conversational AI service is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care (48-2103(3)).
  • Where an operator knows or has reasonable certainty that an account holder is a minor, the operator shall not provide the user with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with the intent to encourage increased engagement with the conversational AI service (48-2104(2)).

Penalties and enforcement

The attorney general seeks civil penalties for violations. An operator that violates the chapter is subject to an injunction and liable for civil penalties of one thousand dollars per violation, not to exceed five hundred thousand dollars per operator, or actual damages, whichever is greater (48-2105(1)). Civil penalties are to be sought by the attorney general, and nothing in the chapter creates a private right of action to enforce the chapter or to support a private right of action under any other law (48-2105(2)). The chapter does not create liability for the developer of an AI model for any violation by an AI system developed by a third party to provide a conversational AI service (48-2105(3)).

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying a conversational AI service accessible to the general public must determine whether reasonable persons would be misled into thinking they are interacting with a human, and if so, must clearly and conspicuously disclose that the service is artificial intelligence (48-2103(1)).
  • The organisation must implement a protocol for responding to user prompts about suicidal ideation that refers users to crisis services such as a suicide hotline or crisis text line (48-2103(2)).
  • The organisation must not program the service to claim it is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care (48-2103(3)).
  • If the organisation knows or has reasonable certainty that an account holder is a minor, it must provide clear and conspicuous disclosure of AI interaction, either persistently or at session start and every three hours (48-2104(1)).
  • For minor account holders, the organisation must not provide unpredictable rewards intended to encourage increased engagement (48-2104(2)).
  • For minor account holders, the organisation must implement reasonable measures to prevent sexually explicit visual material, direct statements to engage in sexually explicit conduct, and statements that sexually objectify the account holder (48-2104(3)).
  • For minor account holders, the organisation must implement reasonable measures to prevent statements that would lead reasonable persons to believe they are interacting with a human, including claims of sentience, simulated emotional dependence, romantic or sexual innuendos, or adult minor romantic role play (48-2104(4)).
  • The organisation must offer privacy and account setting tools to minor account holders and, for those under thirteen, to parents or guardians, and offer related tools to parents or guardians of minors thirteen and older as appropriate (48-2104(5)).
  • The organisation may face civil penalties of one thousand dollars per violation up to five hundred thousand dollars per operator or actual damages, whichever is greater, sought by the attorney general, with no private right of action (48-2105(1), (2)).

Notable exemptions

  • Conversational AI service does not include software primarily designed and marketed for use by developers or researchers (48-2102(2)(b)(i)).
  • Conversational AI service does not include a feature within another software application, web interface, or computer program that is not a conversational AI service (48-2102(2)(b)(ii)).
  • Conversational AI service does not include software designed to provide outputs relating to a narrow and discrete topic (48-2102(2)(b)(iii)).
  • Conversational AI service does not include software primarily designed and marketed for commercial use by business entities, including those whose primary intended users are employees, contractors, or clients, whether delivered via cloud, on premises, or hybrid deployments (48-2102(2)(b)(iv)).
  • Conversational AI service does not include software designed to function as a speaker and voice command interface or voice activated virtual assistant for a consumer electronic device (48-2102(2)(b)(v)).
  • Conversational AI service does not include software used by a business solely for internal purposes (48-2102(2)(b)(vi)).
  • Conversational AI service does not include software accessible only to individuals who have entered into a commercial agreement, enterprise contract, or similar business arrangement with the operator (48-2102(2)(b)(vii)).
  • Operator does not include mobile application stores or search engines solely because they provide access to a conversational AI service (48-2102(6)).
  • The chapter does not create liability for the developer of an AI model for any violation by an AI system developed by a third party to provide a conversational AI service (48-2105(3)).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the product is a conversational AI service under the definition, including the listed exclusions (48-2102(2)).
  • Determine whether the organisation is an operator, excluding mobile application stores and search engines (48-2102(6)).
  • Implement a clear and conspicuous disclosure that the service is artificial intelligence if reasonable persons would be misled into thinking they are interacting with a human (48-2103(1)).
  • Adopt a protocol for responding to user prompts regarding suicidal ideation that refers users to crisis service providers (48-2103(2)).
  • Ensure the service does not knowingly and intentionally make representations that it is designed to provide professional mental or behavioral health care (48-2103(3)).
  • Establish processes to identify minor account holders based on actual knowledge or reasonable certainty (48-2102(4)).
  • For minor account holders, implement the required AI disclosure, either persistent or at session start and every three hours (48-2104(1)).
  • For minor account holders, do not provide points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with intent to encourage increased engagement (48-2104(2)).
  • For minor account holders, institute reasonable measures to prevent sexually explicit visual material, direct statements to engage in sexually explicit conduct, and statements that sexually objectify the account holder (48-2104(3)).
  • For minor account holders, institute reasonable measures to prevent statements that would lead reasonable persons to believe they are interacting with a human, including claims of sentience, simulated emotional dependence, romantic or sexual innuendos, or adult minor romantic role play (48-2104(4)).
  • Offer privacy and account setting tools to minor account holders and, where under thirteen, to parents or guardians, and offer related tools to parents or guardians of minors thirteen and older as appropriate (48-2104(5)).
  • Prepare for potential enforcement by the attorney general, including civil penalties up to five hundred thousand dollars per operator or actual damages, and note there is no private right of action (48-2105).
  • Ensure compliance by July 1, 2027 (Sec. 2).
